knowledge_units.context_summary: The paper introduces Dense-TSNet, an ultra-lightweight speech enhancement network with approximately 14K parameters designed for resource-constrained environments. It utilizes a Dense Two-Stage architecture and a Multi-View Gaze Block (MVGB) based on convolutional neural networks to improve feature extraction and address early convergence issues.

relationships.target: Early convergence limitations of the baseline model

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text introduces Dense-TSNet, an ultra-lightweight speech enhancement network with approximately 14K parameters designed for edge devices. It proposes a Dense Two-Stage (Dense-TS) architecture to address uneven loss landscapes in narrow models and a Multi-View Gaze Block (MVGB) for feature extraction using CNNs. The method utilizes a Consistency Magnitude Loss to improve perceptual quality while avoiding negative impacts on subjective perception associated with Metric Loss.

attributes.target_application: edge devices such as smartphones and cameras
attributes.output: magnitude spectrum mask multiplied by noisy magnitude spectrum

attributes.description: Replaces dilated convolutions in Dilated Dense Block with Two-Stage modules
attributes.purpose: Address loss landscape smoothness in narrow lightweight models

attributes.rationale: Metric Loss may negatively impact subjective perception

attributes.components: Densely connected encoder-decoder with dilated convolutions; Feature extraction layer with serially connected Two-Stage modules
attributes.performance_limitation: Faces limitations for ultra-lightweight networks with narrow architecture due to uneven loss landscapes

attributes.function: Converts speech signal into time-frequency (TF) domain

knowledge_units.context_summary: The Dense-TS architecture modifies the classic Two-Stage structure by replacing dilated dense blocks with densely connected Two-Stage modules to improve loss landscape smoothness in narrow models. The Multi-View Gaze Block (MVGB) extracts global, channel, and local features using Large Kernel Extractor, Channel Attention, and Learnable-Sigmoid Gate sub-modules. The final output is generated by decoding a magnitude spectrum mask via L-Sigmoid activation and 1x1 convolution.

attributes.description: Replaces dilated dense blocks in the encoder with Two-Stage feature extraction blocks using dense connections to merge shallow and deep features

attributes.components: Large Kernel Extractor (LKE), Learnable-Sigmoid Gate (LSG), Channel Attention (CA)
attributes.function: Extracts global, channel, and high-frequency local information
Establishes global perspective and captures long-range low-frequency features
attributes.components: Pointwise convolutions, Simple Gate, large kernel depthwise convolutions, Instance Norm, HardSwish

attributes.function: Reallocates weights to channels to focus on important ones and suppress less significant ones
Establishes local spatial perspectives and enhances high-frequency details
attributes.components: Depth-wise convolution, point-wise convolution, Learnable-Sigmoid activation

attributes.post_processing: L-Sigmoid activation and 1x1 convolution to decode magnitude spectrum mask

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text describes the loss functions and experimental setup for the Dense-TSNet speech enhancement model. It defines a Consistency Magnitude Loss and a Metric Loss based on PESQ, noting that the latter is disabled by default to avoid perceptual degradation. The model is trained on the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset using specific STFT parameters and evaluated against state-of-the-art methods.

attributes.definition: Minimum distance between the magnitude spectrum of twice-STFTed speech and the clean speech magnitude spectrum
Integrates objective evaluation metrics (PESQ) as loss functions via a discriminator

knowledge_units.context_summary: Dense-TSNet outperforms the classic Two-Stage structure in later training stages due to a smoother loss landscape from dense connections. The model achieves competitive performance with only 14K parameters, outperforming heavier models like PHASEN and MANNER-S-5.3GF. Ablation studies confirm the importance of the LKE, CA, and LSG components, while the Metric Loss was excluded due to training instability and perceptual distortions at high weights.

attributes.definition: Metric Loss integrating objective evaluation metrics

relationships.target: amplitude, phase, and complex spectrum errors with P

attributes.function: minimizes distance between estimated and clean magnitude spectra
